rules.episode: A recorded episode starts when one country takes a measure against another (a trade measure aimed at it in Global Trade Alert, a sanctions listing, or a WTO dispute) after at least a year without one, and lasts while measures keep coming less than a year apart.
rules.response: What the target did: measures against the country that started it within a year of the same kind (in kind), of a different kind (another lever), a WTO dispute, or nothing recorded; an episode counts under every way it was answered. Researched episodes add backing down and finding new partners, from news and official sources, over the whole episode. Speed: months to the first answer.
rules.after: After the answer, over the next six months: both sides added measures (escalated), neither did (calmed), or only one did (held). Recorded outcomes count only complete six-month follow-up windows whose records are final (90 days after the last month, as for the forecasts); newer answers remain pending. For researched episodes, the tagged moves after the first answer.
rules.joined: Other countries taking the same kind of measure against the target within three months (joined), or any measure against the country that started it (backed the target). Researched episodes: documented joiners and backers; third parties in a WTO case are counted apart.
rules.researched: Researched episodes are counted only when at least one of their measures is linked to a political dispute by a credible source (level 2); every researched move is shown on the map.
rules.similar: Similar cases: researched episodes between the same two countries, then researched episodes against the same target, then recorded trade-measure episodes against the same target, then all researched episodes, then all recorded trade-measure episodes: the first group with at least five cases.
